claim: Germany’s Foreign Minister Heiko Maas said that Thailand’s King Maha Vajiralongkorn didn’t do anything illegal while at his German residence.
justification: The fact-check refutes the claim because Germany's Foreign Minister Heiko Maas did not exonerate the Thai king; instead, he warned of "immediate consequences" if illegal actions were found. The statement was made in response to parliamentary questions accusing King Maha Vajiralongkorn of conducting politics from Germany, with opposition politicians calling his actions illegal. While German courts have cited laws on diplomatic immunity, no formal legal conclusion of innocence was issued, and the German government's position was explicitly conditional and contested ([Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/10/27/asia-pacific/germany-thailand-king/), [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/europe/thai-king-s-sojourn-in-bavaria-causes-diplomatic-headache-1.4378494)).
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the key finding is that German Foreign Minister Heiko Maas did not assert that the Thai King had not done anything illegal. Instead, in response to parliamentary allegations about the king conducting politics from Germany, Maas stated that the government was "monitoring this long-term" and that there would be "immediate consequences if there are things that we assess to be illegal." The German government's position was explicitly conditional and warned against potential illegality, rather than declaring the king's actions legal.

The evidence clearly contradicts the claim, so no further investigation is needed.

The recorded evidence directly refutes the claim that Heiko Maas stated the king "didn’t do anything illegal." His actual public statements were warnings about potential illegal activity, not affirmations of legality. Therefore, the conclusion is `refuted`.

claim: Officer who wore Trump 2020 mask to polls to face disciplinary action
justification: The claim is supported by photographic evidence, as a photo shared by [Attorney Steve Simeonidis](https://www.clickorlando.com/news/florida/2020/10/20/florida-officer-to-be-disciplined-after-wearing-trump-mask-while-voting/) showed Miami Police Officer Daniel Ubeda in uniform wearing a "Trump 2020" mask inside an early voting site in Miami on October 20, 2020. The Miami Police Department, led by [Police Chief Jorge Colina](https://www.theledger.com/story/news/state/2020/10/20/miami-police-officer-daniel-ubeda-spotted-wearing-trump-mask-in-uniform-early-voting-site-florida/5994006002/), confirmed the behavior was "unacceptable" and a violation of departmental policy, and that disciplinary action was being addressed, as also noted by [Miami Mayor Francis Suarez](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2020/10/20/miami-police-officer-trump-2020-mask-poll-discipline/6001128002/).
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the fact-check has established that Miami Police Officer Daniel Ubeda was photographed wearing a "Trump 2020" mask while in uniform at an early voting site in Miami, Florida, on October 20, 2020. Multiple sources, including official statements from the Miami Police Department and its chief, confirm the incident was deemed "unacceptable," a "violation of departmental policy," and that disciplinary action is "being addressed immediately."

The evidence from the fact-check directly and authoritatively verifies every key element of the claim: the officer's action, his identity, his department, the location, and the initiation of disciplinary proceedings. There is no conflicting information or lack of clarity that would require further investigation.

`supported`

claim: Hunter Biden was chairman of the Nobel Peace Prize winning World Food Program.
justification: The fact-check reveals that while Hunter Biden served as **Board Chairman of World Food Program USA**, a separate U.S.-based nonprofit that supports the [United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/world-food-program-wins-2020-nobel-peace-prize-n1242678), he did not hold a leadership role at the Nobel Peace Prize-winning UN agency itself. The [2020 Nobel Peace Prize](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/world-food-program-wins-2020-nobel-peace-prize-n1242678) was awarded to the UN WFP, whose [governance structure](https://executiveboard.wfp.org/about-board) does not include a "chairman" position, and [public records](https://sanantonioreport.org/before-hunter-biden-there-was-billy-carter-neil-bush-and-others/world-food-program-usas-annual-mcgovern-dole-leadership-award-ceremony/) confirm his chairmanship was with the affiliated U.S. organization, not the UN body.
judge_reasoning:
The fact-check reveals a clear distinction between two organizations: the United Nations World Food Programme (UN WFP), which won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020, and World Food Program USA, a separate U.S.-based nonprofit that supports the UN agency. Evidence confirms Hunter Biden served as Board Chairman of World Food Program USA, not of the UN WFP itself. While a source notes Hunter Biden once claimed to be chairman of the "U.N. World Food Program," official records and documentation attribute that leadership role within the U.S. organization to him, not the UN entity.

The evidence is sufficient to conclude that the claim incorrectly conflates Hunter Biden's role with the Nobel-winning UN agency. No further investigation is needed because the record establishes a direct factual mismatch: he chaired the U.S.-based support organization, not the UN body that received the prize.

Therefore, the claim that "Hunter Biden was chairman of the Nobel Peace Prize winning World Food Program" is `refuted` because the evidence explicitly shows he held a leadership position in a different, affiliated organization.

claim: Joe and Jill Biden's income has increased recently.
justification: The claim is supported by multiple credible reports showing that Joe and Jill Biden's income spiked dramatically in 2017 and 2018, following his departure from the vice presidency. Their adjusted gross income rose from about $396,000 in 2016 to over $11 million in 2017 and $4.6 million in 2018, a surge primarily attributable to substantial earnings from book deals for his work *Promise Me, Dad* and from a series of paid speaking engagements, with individual fees reportedly reaching as high as $190,000. This data is documented in their released tax returns and covered by sources including [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/09/joe-biden-releases-tax-returns-during-2020-democratic-primary.html), [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/joe-jill-biden-reported-earning-15-million-income/story?id=64225419), and the [San Diego Union-Tribune](https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/us-politics/la-na-pol-2020-joe-biden-income-20190709-story.html).
judge_reasoning:
The fact-check confirms a clear and substantial increase in Joe and Jill Biden's income. Specifically, their adjusted gross income jumped from about $396,000 in 2016 to over $11 million in 2017 and $4.6 million in 2018. This spike is well-documented and attributed to earnings from book deals and paid speaking engagements after Joe Biden left the vice presidency.

The evidence from multiple credible sources is consistent and provides precise figures for the relevant timeframe, leaving no ambiguity. Therefore, no further investigation is needed.

`supported`

claim: A “new virus” disease called Novel Bunya V!rus that is caused by ticks is diagnosed as severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is spreading in China.
justification: Based on the fact-check record, the claim is supported. The SFTS virus (SFTSV) is officially classified as a type of bunyavirus, specifically a phlebovirus ([BMC Infectious Diseases](https://bmcinfectdis.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12879-020-05072-w)), and is a tick-borne pathogen ([PLOS NTDs](https://journals.plos.org/plosntds/article?id=10.1371/journal.pntd.0004574)). While the term "Novel Bunya Virus" is not an official designation, Chinese and international reports consistently use it to refer to SFTSV, which was identified in 2009 ([Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/content/1196864.shtml)) and is recognized as a novel emerging virus by bodies like the ECDC ([ECDC](https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/news-events/fever-thrombocytopenia-associated-novel-bunyavirus-china)). The disease is not new but is an established, spreading infection in China, with cases documented across multiple provinces including Henan, Shandong, Hubei, Anhui, and Zhejiang ([PLOS NTDs](https://journals.plos.org/plosntds/article?id=10.1371/journal.pntd.0008186)), and has been reported for over a decade ([BMC Infectious Diseases](https://bmcinfectdis.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12879-020-05303-0)).
judge_reasoning:
**Summary of Key Insights:**  
The fact-check confirms that the SFTS virus (SFTSV) is a tick-borne bunyavirus causing severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and it has been spreading in China since at least 2009, with over 5,000 cases reported by 2016 across 23 provinces. While the term "Novel Bunya Virus" is not an official WHO or China CDC designation, it is used in Chinese medical reports to describe SFTSV. The virus was indeed identified as novel around 2009–2011, but it is not a newly emerging pathogen; it has been documented for over a decade with seasonal peaks.

**Missing Information:**  
No critical information is lacking—the evidence clearly addresses the virus type, transmission, spread, and timeline. Further investigation is not needed.

**Conclusion:**  
Based on the evidence, the claim that a "new virus" called Novel Bunya Virus, caused by ticks and diagnosed as SFTS, is spreading in China is **largely supported** in substance, though the descriptor "new" is misleading as SFTSV has been known since 2009. The core facts about the virus and its spread align with recorded data. Therefore, the decision is `supported`.

claim: There is more chance of an asteroid hitting Earth on 02/11/2020 than dying from COVID-19.
justification: The claim is refuted because NASA's data indicates the probability of a significant asteroid impact on any given day, including November 2, 2020, is negligibly small, whereas the documented risk of death from COVID-19, even for younger populations in early pandemic epicenters, was substantially higher. The comparison is also invalid as it mixes an instantaneous daily risk (asteroid) with a cumulative infection or case fatality risk (COVID-19) calculated over a different timeframe.
judge_reasoning:
## Step 1: Summary of Key Insights

The fact-check reveals that the claim's comparison is fundamentally flawed. NASA states that no asteroid larger than 140 meters has a "significant" chance of hitting Earth for the next 100 years, making the probability of an asteroid impact on any specific day like 02/11/2020 negligibly small. The asteroid most associated with that date—2018 VP1—was only about 2 meters in diameter and had roughly a 0.41% chance of entering Earth's atmosphere, where it would have disintegrated harmlessly. Meanwhile, COVID-19 death probabilities were measurable and substantial: the WHO estimated an IFR of approximately 0.5–1%, and even for younger, low-risk populations, the absolute mortality risk was estimated at 10–349 per million (roughly 1 in 100,000 to 1 in 2,865). For elderly populations, risks were far higher. The COVID-19 death risk, even in the most favorable demographic, was orders of magnitude greater than any asteroid impact probability on that date.

## Step 2: Missing Information

The evidence is sufficiently clear. No further investigation is needed—the asteroid probability is negligibly small by authoritative estimates, and COVID-19 mortality risk is well-documented and clearly higher.

## Step 3: Conclusion

The claim asserts that there was a greater chance of an asteroid hitting Earth on 02/11/2020 than of dying from COVID-19. The evidence clearly contradicts this: the asteroid impact probability on that specific date was negligibly small according to NASA, while COVID-19 mortality risk—even for the lowest-risk demographic—was significantly higher. Therefore, the claim is `refuted`.

claim: Amy Coney Barrett has a written track record, disagreeing adamantly with the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision to uphold the Affordable Care Act.
justification: The fact-check confirms Amy Coney Barrett's "written track record" of disagreeing with the Supreme Court's rulings upholding the Affordable Care Act, as documented in a [2017 Notre Dame Law School article](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/supreme-court/trump-scotus-pick-amy-coney-barrett-s-past-critiques-obamacare-n1241191) and a [book review](https://capaction.medium.com/amy-coney-barrett-is-a-targeted-missile-at-the-affordable-care-act-and-protections-for-people-with-dd06c610e20). In these works, she explicitly criticized the legal reasoning in both *NFIB v. Sebelius* (2012) and *King v. Burwell* (2015), stating Chief Justice Roberts "pushed the Affordable Care Act beyond its plausible meaning to save the statute" and arguing it is "illegitimate for the Court to distort either the Constitution or a statute to achieve what it deems a preferable result." This critical pattern was verified by legal scholars, supporting the claim.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the fact-check has established that Amy Coney Barrett authored a 2017 law review article in which she explicitly and strongly criticized the Supreme Court's reasoning in the 2012 *NFIB v. Sebelius* decision, stating that Chief Justice Roberts "pushed the Affordable Care Act beyond its plausible meaning to save the statute." She further argued that it is "illegitimate for the Court to distort either the Constitution or a statute to achieve what it deems a preferable result." The evidence also shows she wrote favorably of the dissent in the 2015 *King v. Burwell* case.

The evidence is clear and comprehensive, providing direct quotes from her written work that demonstrate substantive disagreement with the legal foundations of the Court's ACA rulings. No further investigation is required.

The claim states Amy Coney Barrett has a "written track record" of disagreeing "adamantly" with the Supreme Court's decisions upholding the ACA. The documented evidence shows she authored formal, published work explicitly and forcefully criticizing the legal reasoning of those decisions. Her choice of words, such as "illegitimate" and "distort," supports the characterization of adamant disagreement. Therefore, the knowledge from the fact-check supports the Claim.

`supported`

claim: Americans advised to reconsider travel to Ghana due to COVID-19.
justification: The U.S. Department of State issued a [Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory](https://web.archive.org/web/20210122073123/https://gh.usembassy.gov/travel-alert-092220/) for Ghana, updated on September 22, 2020, citing COVID-19 concerns. The advisory applied to the entire country (though certain regions were separately flagged for crime-related risks) and was supported by the CDC's Level 3 Travel Health Notice. Ghana at the time had reported over 32,000 confirmed cases and 168 deaths, with one of the highest testing rates in Africa, according to [Brookings](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/how-well-is-ghana-with-one-of-the-best-testing-capacities-in-africa-responding-to-covid-19/). The advisory came with specific guidance, including requirements for negative PCR tests, on-arrival testing, and mandatory mask-wearing, as detailed by the [Ghana Consulate](https://www.ghanaconsulatear.org/travel-advisories/). Similar guidance was issued by the [UK FCDO](https://www.fitfortravel.nhs.uk/destinations/africa/ghana), and the advisory had tangible effects, such as the [temporary suspension of visa processing services](https://www.passporthealthusa.com/passports-and-visas/visas/ghana-visa/). The claim is **supported**.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the key finding is that the U.S. Department of State officially issued a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" advisory for Ghana, explicitly due to the COVID-19 pandemic, as documented on the U.S. Embassy in Ghana's archived webpage dated September 22, 2020. The advisory directly links to the CDC's Travel Health Notice and includes specific entry requirements related to COVID-19, confirming the pandemic as the primary reason for the advisory level.

The evidence is clear and directly supports the claim, so no further investigation is required. The recorded sources, including the official embassy page, unambiguously state that Americans were advised to "Reconsider Travel" to Ghana because of COVID-19.

`supported`

claim: Ventura County election officials are reducing voting locations in order to limit in-person voter turnout.
justification: The reduction from 389 to 47 in-person locations was implemented as part of a broader, state-mandated shift to a [Voting Center model](https://www.sos.ca.gov/voters-choice-act) and was publicly justified by officials as a [COVID-19 safety measure](https://www.mpacorn.com/articles/mail-in-voter-fraud-the-faulty-premise-behind-the-claim/) to encourage vote-by-mail, not to limit turnout. Officials added 30 ballot drop boxes and extended in-person voting hours over four days, explicitly stating the remaining locations were for voters who [needed that option](https://www.mpacorn.com/articles/mail-in-voter-fraud-the-faulty-premise-behind-the-claim/), with no evidence of an intent to suppress in-person voting.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the fact-check reveals that while Ventura County significantly reduced the number of traditional polling places from 389 in March 2020 to 47 in November 2020, the stated reasons for this change were to accommodate the COVID-19 pandemic and to align with a state-mandated shift toward a vote center model under California's Voter's Choice Act. Officials explicitly encouraged mail-in voting and expanded alternative voting access through additional ballot drop boxes and extended early voting hours. There is no evidence in the provided sources to suggest the reduction was intended to limit in-person voter turnout; rather, it was presented as a modernization and safety measure.

The evidence is sufficiently clear on the stated intent of the officials, so no further investigation is required to address the claim's core assertion about motivation.

The claim that officials reduced voting locations "in order to limit in-person voter turnout" is not supported by the evidence. The recorded reasons for the reduction (public health, state policy shift, and encouraging mail-in voting) explicitly contradict the claimed intent to suppress turnout. Therefore, the conclusion is that the claim is `refuted`.

claim: US state of Georgia has “almost 100,000 more COVID-19 cases, almost twice as many deaths and almost 600 more nursing home deaths than North Carolina, US.
justification: The claim that Georgia had nearly 100,000 more COVID-19 cases than North Carolina is contradicted by the evidence: as of late May 2020, Georgia had [39,801 confirmed cases](https://www.savannahnow.com/story/news/coronavirus/2020/05/20/georgia-covid-19-cases-rise-by-946-since-tuesday-to-total-39801/1173036007/) while North Carolina had [22,725 confirmed cases](https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/05/23/861561659/north-carolina-reports-highest-one-day-spike-of-covid-19-cases), a difference of roughly 17,000 — far short of 100,000. Regarding deaths, Georgia had [1,697 cumulative deaths](https://www.savannahnow.com/story/news/coronavirus/2020/05/20/georgia-covid-19-cases-rise-by-946-since-tuesday-to-total-39801/1173036007/) as of May 20, 2020, but the only available North Carolina death figure cited ([10 deaths as of April 1, 2020](https://www.northcarolinahealthnews.org/2020/04/01/coronavirus-today-april-1/)) comes from a much earlier date, making a direct comparison unreliable, and the "almost twice as many deaths" assertion cannot be substantiated with comparable data. On nursing home deaths, Georgia reported [more than 2,000](https://www.georgiahealthnews.com/2020/08/nursing-home-chain-suffers-big-toll-covid/), while North Carolina reported [more than 150 deaths](https://carolinapublicpress.org/30369/dhhs-reverses-stance-on-identifying-nursing-homes-with-outbreaks/) across all congregate living settings — a gap far exceeding "almost 600." Overall, the claim's specific numerical comparisons do not align with the available data.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the claim that Georgia had "almost 100,000 more COVID-19 cases" than North Carolina is clearly refuted, as the documented case counts show a difference of approximately 17,000 cases (Georgia ~39,801 vs. North Carolina ~22,725), which is far from 100,000. The other parts of the claim regarding deaths and nursing home deaths cannot be conclusively evaluated due to mismatched dates and incomplete data; for instance, the death figures for North Carolina are from a much earlier period, making a valid comparison impossible.

The evidence provided is insufficient to verify the comparisons for total deaths and nursing home deaths, as the data points are not contemporaneous or are overly vague (e.g., North Carolina's nursing home deaths are grouped with other congregate settings). Therefore, a definitive decision on those aspects cannot be made.

Given that the case count comparison is explicitly and significantly incorrect, the claim is not supported. The final decision is `refuted`.

claim: Schools have resumed in New Brunswick, Canada despite the COVID-19 pandemic
justification: The claim that schools resumed in New Brunswick, Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic is **SUPPORTED**. The New Brunswick government officially announced that [schools would resume in September 2020](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/coronavirus-covid-19-schools-1.5575660), with Education Minister Dominic Cardy confirming teachers would return between June 1-5 to prepare and familiarize themselves with new safety protocols. Schools had initially [closed on March 16, 2020](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/covid-19-new-brunswick-coronavirus-1.5496547) for at least two weeks due to the pandemic. The reopening included mandated health measures such as daily face masks, physical distancing, reduced class sizes, increased cleaning, and replacing water fountains with bottle filling stations. The decision was met with support from the teacher union, with the president of the New Brunswick Teachers' Association [approving the province's back-to-school plan](https://atlantic.ctvnews.ca/n-b-teachers-generally-approve-of-province-s-back-to-school-plan-1.5066662) and noting the regular involvement of public health officials as encouraging.
judge_reasoning:
## Step 1: Summary of Key Insights

The evidence gathered indicates that schools in New Brunswick, Canada, were initially closed on March 16, 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In late April 2020, the government announced schools would not reopen until September at the earliest. Education Minister Dominic Cardy confirmed that "school will resume in September" and organized teachers' return between June 1 and June 5, 2020, to prepare for the fall. Detailed health and safety protocols were established—including mandatory face masks, physical distancing, reduced class sizes, increased cleaning, and other measures—constituting a comprehensive "back-to-school plan." The New Brunswick Teachers' Association president expressed support for the plan, noting its "regular involvement of public health in all aspects."

## Step 2: Remaining Gaps

The evidence does not include an explicit confirmation that schools physically opened their doors on a specific date in September 2020. However, the existence of a detailed, approved back-to-school plan with specific safety protocols, the teacher union's endorsement, and the minister's stated intention to resume in September collectively create a strong chain of evidence that the resumption occurred as planned.

## Step 3: Conclusion

The claim states that "Schools have resumed in New Brunswick, Canada despite the COVID-19 pandemic." The recorded evidence shows that the provincial government authorized a return to school for September 2020, established specific safety protocols, and gained the approval of the teacher union for the plan. While an exact reopening date is not explicitly cited in the retrieved articles, the convergence of the government's announced plan, the detailed operational protocols, and the institutional support for the return strongly implies that schools did resume during the pandemic. Therefore, my decision is `supported`.

claim: Viral message claims that all Haldiram’s food products were banned in USA
justification: The viral claim is refuted by [NewsMeter's fact-check](https://newsmeter.in/fact-check-viral-message-that-all-haldirams-food-products-were-banned-in-usa-is-false/), which determined the message is false. While the U.S. FDA has indeed [refused entry to specific Haldiram's shipments](https://www.scoopwhoop.com/news/after-maggi-haldiram/) on multiple occasions due to detected pesticides, mold, and salmonella, these actions were targeted at individual product consignments rather than constituting a blanket ban on all Haldiram's products. [Haldiram's has dismissed the allegations](https://www.scoopwhoop.com/news/after-maggi-haldiram/), asserting that its food is safe and complies with applicable laws. Furthermore, Haldiram's products remain commercially available in the U.S., as evidenced by a [deal with Amazon](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-jeff-bezos-brings-haldiram-to-us-customers-now-buy-bhujia-in-america-thanks-to-amazon-1755825/) that allows American consumers to purchase items such as bhujia and gulab jamun online. No U.S. law, regulation, or executive order names Haldiram's as a completely banned entity, confirming that the viral message conflated targeted import refusals with a nonexistent total prohibition.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the fact-check, the key evidence demonstrates that while a viral message claiming all Haldiram's products were banned in the USA does exist, authoritative sources—including a dedicated fact-check—conclude this claim is false. The evidence shows the U.S. FDA has refused entry to specific Haldiram's shipments due to issues like pesticides and salmonella, but this represents targeted regulatory actions against certain products, not a blanket ban. Furthermore, Haldiram's products remain available for purchase in the U.S., and the company has officially denied the claim.

The evidence is clear and consistent across multiple sources, leaving no substantial information gaps that require further investigation.

`refuted`

claim: Some US mayors are fining people for going to church during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Given the documented incidents, the claim is **SUPPORTED**.
judge_reasoning:
The fact-check confirms that at least one U.S. mayor—Lori Lightfoot of Chicago—authorized fines in connection with in-person church services during the COVID-19 pandemic. In May 2020, three Chicago churches were each fined $500 for violating a state stay-at-home order that limited gatherings to more than ten people. While the fines were issued to the churches as institutions for breaching a general public health order—not specifically to individual attendees for the act of going to church—the documented enforcement action was directly targeted at congregations for holding religious services.

The evidence is sufficient to evaluate the claim, as it provides a clear, documented instance of a U.S. mayor implementing fines in response to in-person church attendance. The nuance is that the fines were levied on the churches themselves for violating gathering restrictions, not on individuals merely for attending. However, the claim’s phrasing ("fining people for going to church") is reasonably interpreted as the enforcement action being directed at the activity of attending church, which the evidence supports.

`supported`

claim: 558 people were killed by the police in 2018, while 201 people died in police custody

According to [The Washington Post's database](https://archive.investigativereportingworkshop.org/investigation/police-shot-killed-nearly-1000-in-2018/) as reported by the Investigative Reporting Workshop, police fatally shot 998 people in the U.S. in 2018—nearly double the claimed 558. For deaths in police custody, the monitoring organization [INQUEST](https://www.inquest.org.uk/deaths-in-police-custody) reported only 20 such deaths in England and Wales in 2018, a fraction of the claimed 201. Additionally, other U.S.-focused sources like [The Root](https://www.theroot.com/here-s-how-many-people-police-killed-in-2018-1831469528) cite even higher police killing figures for 2018, further contradicting the claim.

The fact-check reveals that for the United States in 2018, multiple credible sources report a number of people killed by police substantially higher than the claimed 558, with figures ranging from approximately 986 to 1,165. For deaths in police custody, the only specific evidence found pertains to England and Wales, where the 2018 figure was 20, which is drastically lower than the claimed 201. No evidence was found to support the claim's specific numbers for any single, clearly defined jurisdiction.

While the claim does not specify a jurisdiction, the evidence strongly contradicts the figure of 558 police killings for the United States, the most likely implied context. No supporting evidence was found for either statistic, and the available evidence for the presumed context for each part of the claim points to significantly different numbers. Therefore, based on the recorded evidence, the claim is not supported.

`refuted`

justification: While Donald Trump did sign [four executive orders on July 24, 2020](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/07/24/trump-announces-series-of-executive-orders-aimed-at-lowering-drug-costs.html), they were [directives for future agency rulemaking, not immediately enforceable laws](https://www.ebglaw.com/insights/publications/president-trump-signs-executive-orders-on-drug-pricing-and-domestic-supply-chain-reform). Experts were [skeptical of their potential impact](https://www.healthevolution.com/insider/breaking-down-the-trump-administrations-executive-orders-on-drug-pricing/), and pharmaceutical groups [strongly opposed them](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/07/24/trump-announces-series-of-executive-orders-aimed-at-lowering-drug-costs.html). Subsequent data showed [no evidence of the claimed massive price reductions](https://www.boston.com/news/politics/2019/05/14/ap-fact-check-trump-cites-drug-price-drop-that-isnt/), confirming the orders did not substantively lower consumer costs.
judge_reasoning:
Based on the recorded evidence, the key finding is that Donald Trump did sign four executive orders on July 24, 2020, aimed at lowering prescription drug costs. However, these orders were not immediately effective laws but directives for future agency rulemaking, which faced significant implementation challenges. Expert analyses were skeptical of their potential impact, and subsequent price data showed prescription drug costs increased, not massively decreased.

The information needed to finalize the check with absolute certainty is already provided: the evidence is clear that the executive orders did not result in the claimed "massive" reduction in drug costs.

Therefore, the claim that the signed orders "would massively lower the cost" of prescription drugs is not supported by the available evidence. While the signing of the orders is factual, the consequential claim of a massive cost reduction is refuted by expert assessments and subsequent price data showing no such outcome. The final decision is `refuted`.
